Five lens percentiles in order G E M P V, each 0-99 in today's GMV universe (NASDAQ / NYSE / AMEX, market cap at least $1B). G growth, E estimates, M momentum, P participation (volume), V value. Each lens is the median percentile of its own parts; -- means fewer than two parts were present. Lenses are never added together.
The profile that brought the name into Focus: its first place in the round-robin (rank 1 of every long profile, then rank 2, and so on).
Every long profile (COMPOUNDER, RERATE, BREAKOUT, VALUE_TURN, ALL5) the name ranked in after the industry cap, comma-separated.
The GMV profile this row belongs to.
The profile's weakest lens percentile (0-1) for this name. The profile sorts on it, ties on the mean of the same lenses. For FADE it is the weakest of 1 - M, 1 - E and 1 - P.
Letter of the name's lowest lens percentile (G, E, M, P or V).
Letter of the name's highest lens percentile.
Label from trend_q, r_1m and hi_prox (bands in config/generic_utils/gmv_lens.json). Not a rank.
tape_state: trend_q at least 0.35, not PULLBACK or EXTENDED.
tape_state: trend_q at least 0.35 and r_1m at most -4%. An uptrend that is giving back this month.
tape_state: trend_q at least 0.35, hi_prox at least -2% (at or near the 91-day high) and r_1m at least 15%.
tape_state: trend_q between -0.35 and 0.35. No clear trend.
tape_state: trend_q at most -0.35.
tape_state: fewer than 20 snapshots in the 91-day window, so no trend fit.
Profile, mid term: weakest of G, E and M. Growth that estimates and the tape both confirm. Value is shown, not used.
Profile, mid term: weakest of G, E and V. Growth with rising estimates that still trades cheap to peers. Momentum is not used, so many are early or still falling.
Profile, short term: weakest of M, P and E. Trend with volume behind it and estimates moving up. A trade, not a valuation call.
Profile, short to mid term: weakest of V, E and P. Cheap names where estimates turn up and buyers come back. The rebound case with evidence.
Profile, mid term: weakest of all five lenses. No weak lens.
Profile, short term, inverted: weakest of 1 - M, 1 - E and 1 - P. Weak trend, falling estimates and sellers in control together. Short candidates, not an automatic short.
Close versus the snapshot about 30 calendar days earlier, %. Split-adjusted all-fields snapshots.
Close versus the snapshot about 91 calendar days earlier, %.
Signed R squared of ln(close) on calendar day over the last 91 days: the sign of the slope times R squared. +1 is a straight rising line, -1 a straight falling one, near 0 no trend.
Annualized slope of the trend_q fit, %.
r_3m divided by (vol_d x square root of 63): the 3-month return in units of the name's own daily volatility. The only place volatility enters a lens, as a denominator.
Close versus the highest close of the last 91 days, %. 0 is at the high.

Last 30 days: summed relative volume on up days divided by summed relative volume on down days (day change field). Above 1 is heavier volume on up days. Relative volume is read at scan time, so intraday snapshots add noise.
Last 91 days: sum of sign(day change) x relative volume, divided by summed relative volume. -1 to 1; positive is accumulation.
10-day average volume versus 30-day average volume, %.
Standard deviation of the daily change field over 91 days, %. Size, not quality. Never a lens of its own.
ATRP x square root of 20, %. Size of a typical 20-day move. Not a direction.
Street revenue forecast for the next fiscal year versus trailing 12-month revenue, %.
Street EPS forecast for the next fiscal year versus trailing diluted EPS, %. Blank when either is at or under 0.
Trailing 12-month revenue growth year over year, %.
Trailing diluted EPS growth year over year, %.

Next-FY EPS forecast, same window: (up steps - down steps) divided by steps that moved. -1 to 1.
Compounded change of the next-FY revenue forecast over about 91 days, %. Same roll rule as eps_rev_3m.
Average price target now versus about 91 days ago, %.
Last reported quarter's EPS surprise, % (eps_surprise_percent_fq).

pe_nfy divided by fwd_eps_g. Lower is cheaper growth. Blank when growth is at or under 0.

Cell 'drawdown x letters': dd | the exact det letters.
Change on the scan day against the prior close, % (an intraday scan carries the move so far).
The Book line's value against its cost, %: the paper gain or loss (generic_utils.recovery_ladder).
Average buy price of the line in its quote currency (holdings file): the break-even price.
Rise from the close back to the average price (break-even), % with no add; negative = the line is in profit.
The price at which the line makes the named gain on its (new) average: average x (1 + g/100). gain10 = +10% on the whole line.
Rise needed from the close (or, _from_add, from the add's buy price) to reach gain<g>_px, %.

USD to add at solve_at_px (the bounce band top, else the close) so that a return to the named level breaks the whole line even. 0 = the level is already above the average; empty = the level is not above the buy price, so no add can do it.
The price the scenario add buys at: close (today's mark), bounce_high (top of the buy-in-red band), bounce_low (bottom of it).
The line's average price after buying add_usd at add_px (quote currency).
How much the add lowers the average, % (new_avg vs the old average).
Rise from the add's buy price back to the new average (break-even after the add), %.
The new break-even against the named level, %: under 0 = a return to that level repairs the line.
USD the add alone loses if the price falls from add_px to the kill.
USD the whole line (old shares plus the add) loses from add_px to the kill.
The buy price (and its source level) used to solve add_be_at_<level>_usd.
Close against its 200-day average (vs200 cut at 0): 'over 200d' or 'under 200d'. Empty when there is no 200-day average (config/generic_utils/deterioration.json).
That cell's mean excess return over the horizon (7d / 28d / 56d), percent over the day's US $2B+ median, winsorized. Evidence for the state, not a forecast for the name.
t of the cell's daily mean excess on non-overlapping days only (a day, not a row, is the unit: names of one day move together). Empty under 3 such days; 56d is direction only.
t of the cell's daily means over every day, Newey-West lag = the horizon in files. Higher than the non-overlapping t; trust the smaller.
How many non-overlapping days back the t (one per horizon length).
Share of the cell's rows that beat the median over the horizon.
10th (90th) percentile of the cell's excess return over the horizon, percent: the bad (good) case.
Share of the cell whose raw return over the horizon was -10% or worse (further deterioration in price).
Share of the cell whose raw return over the horizon was +10% or better.
Share of the cell that regained half the gap to its 52-week high by the horizon (close at or above half_px). How often a drawdown repairs inside two months.
Rows (name-days) in the cell with a 28-day (7d / 56d) label; days = distinct store days in the cell.
That cell's mean raw return over the horizon, percent (not against the market).

Book dollars x the cnt cell's mean excess over the horizon / 100: what the median-relative drift of this state was worth on the line, dollars. Negative = the state cost money against the market. Not a forecast, not a size.
Book dollars x the cnt cell's q10 excess over the horizon / 100: the bad case on this line, dollars.
Book line cost in USD (unrealized P&L in USD) from the pack book.
Realized daily volatility over the last 20 day files, %.
A panel-store feature (config/generic_utils/panel_store.json features) read as a factor: its cross-sectional rank on the floor and its signal-lab IC.
The Book's NAV-weighted cross-sectional percentile of the factor (0..1) among the store day's US $2B+ names; 0.5 = the median name. US store lines only (coverage_pct).
book_pctl - 0.5: how far the Book leans high (+) or low (-) on the factor against the median name.
Share of the Book's dollars the read covers, %: lines in the US store (and, per factor, with a value). XETR / OMXCOP lines have no percentile.
The factor's full-sample signal-lab IC at 28 days (daily Spearman vs the later excess return), its verdict and non-overlapping t (factor_summary).
Mean daily 7-day IC in the newest calendar month with labels (month) and the month before (factor_month): what the factor paid lately.
Mean daily 7-day IC over the last 20 labelled days (ending tape_last; labels lag a week) and the 20 days before: is the factor's payoff turning.
Share of those last 20 days with a positive IC.
gap x ic_month (x ic_tape): + = the Book's lean on this factor was paid lately, - = it cost. One factor at a time; never summed into a score.
Median return of the store day's US $2B+ names over the horizon, %.
Median return of the line's industry on the floor over the horizon, % (industries with fewer than 5 names: empty).
Return minus the market median, percentage points (book_rel: NAV-weighted over the Book's US lines).
Industry part: the industry median minus the market median, pp. What being in that industry did (book_ind_part: NAV-weighted).
Stock part: the line's return minus its industry median, pp. What the pick did inside its industry (book_stock_part: NAV-weighted).
Today's line dollars x that part / 100, summed over the Book's US lines: an approximation of what the part cost or earned (today's weights, not the path).
The name's cross-sectional percentile (0..1) of that factor on the store day's floor.
Change in the Book's book_pctl for that factor if a third of this line were sold (trim_frac in pathway.json). Negative on beta = the trim lowers the Book's beta.
Change in the Book's book_pctl for that factor if a $5,000 line in this name were added (starter_usd in pathway.json).
Median 1-month return of the floor that store day, % (the regime field: above 0 = up month); mkt_1d is the median day change.
Share of the floor up on the day.
Share of the floor closing above its 200-day average.
Median realized 20-day volatility, % (median close vs the 52-week high, %) of the floor.
Mean of that factor's daily 7-day IC over the 20 labelled days ending that day: positive = high values have been leading.
The name's industry in the alpha model's month-ahead read (week_plays month_ind): median pred_28d, mean decile, median trailing month. A regime guide, not a buy list.

Pointer cell (print-night matrix): the lift, in percentage points, of the quintile (category for slot / mix) this name sits in on that pointer, against every other past print, on the row's measure. ▲ / ▼ = the direction is clear; a bare number = measured but not clear; empty = no value, or the pointer is not read on that measure (a field is never measured on itself; the print rewrites estimates and the last surprise, so those are empty on printed rows). The field, bucket edges and the cell's n / mean / hit are on the Pointer evidence tab.

The pointer's cell points up / down: |lift_t| at or above t_min (recipe, 2.0) on at least min_n prints (40), the same sign in both halves of the sample (split at the median print date) and the cell's hit rate moving the same way as its mean (so a few large moves cannot set it). Green / red shading is the arrow, not Heat. Many cells are tested and prints cluster by date and industry: an arrow is a measured lean, not a forecast.

Count of pointers whose cell points up (▲) / down (▼) on one measure: rx = the reaction session vs the market; h7 / h28 = held from the close before the print for 7 / 28 days, excess; ac = the reaction close minus the after-hours read (AMC); d28 = drift 28 days from the reaction close. ptr_up / ptr_dn = the same count on a matrix row. A count of measured cells, not a score and not a sum of lifts.

Big-move odds (recipe tail_measures). u10 = the reaction session at +10 pp or more vs the market, d10 = at -10 pp or less, as 0/1 per past print, so a cell's mean is the share of prints that moved that far (base about 10% / 9%). u10_up = pointers whose cell raises the +10 odds (same t / n / halves / hit rules as every arrow); d10_up = pointers that raise the -10 odds (up here means more likely to drop hard). Most size pointers raise both; upside lean = u10_up with d10_up 0. A highlight beside the counts, never a gate, a size or a course.

The highest +10 pp (u10_hi) / -10 pp (d10_hi) reaction odds among the name's measured pointer cells with at least min_n prints, as a share (0.17 = 17% of past prints in that cell moved that far); *_hi_ptr names the pointer. One cell's odds, not a combined probability: read the two side by side. The size read: on 4 Nov 2026 out of sample (179 reporters), u10_hi >= 0.16 moved 6.2% on average after hours (16% moved 10%+ either way), 0.13-0.16 moved 2.7%, under 0.13 moved 1.2%.

Tail balance: +1 per past print at +10 pp or more vs the market, -1 at -10 pp or less, 0 between, so a cell's mean is the up odds minus the down odds (the side of a big move). b10_up / b10_dn = pointers whose cell tilts big moves up / down (same arrow rules); b10_hi = the best balance among the name's cells and b10_hi_ptr its pointer. Few cells clear the rules and the up ones are mostly momentum; on 4 Nov 2026 the up-tilt group had the most -10 nights. Unproven live: a reading, never a call.

Size family pointers, measured on the big-move odds (u10 / d10) only so they never change the rx / h7 / h28 counts: own_abs = mean |reaction vs the market| of the name's earlier lab prints; mcap = market cap before the print; rev_yoy = revenue growth year on year.

How many pointer families (Tape, History, Estimates, Street, Value, Model, Peers, Size; Print, Session after the print) the up / down pointers come from. Run-up, the month, RSI and the 50-day distance are one family and often point together: 3 up from one family is one bet, 3 from three families is three.
The pointers behind the up / down count, by key (their fields on the Pointer evidence tab).

A field known at the time (before the print: tape, history, estimates, street, value, model, peers; after it: surprise, mix, after-hours read, reaction) cut into quintiles on the lab's past prints; recipe config/generic_utils/print_night.json.
The quintile (Q1 lowest .. Q5 highest, with its edges [low, high) from the past prints) or the category (slot, mix) a value sits in.

What a cell is measured on: react_fx (rx), hold_fx_7d (h7), hold_fx_28d (h28) before the print; react_fx, ah_to_close (ac), drift_fx_28d (d28) after it. code is the short name used in the count columns.
The cell's mean minus the mean of every other past print on the same measure, percentage points. Positive = prints in this cell did better than the rest.
Welch t of the lift (cell vs the rest). Prints are treated as independent, so it is optimistic; the halves and hit rules guard it.
The lift inside the earlier and the later half of the sample (split at the median print date). An arrow needs both on the same side as the full lift.
The cell's share of positive prints minus the rest's. An arrow needs it on the same side as the lift: the typical print moved, not only the average.
up / down = the cell's direction is clear (see ▲ / ▼); - = measured without a clear direction; empty = no cell (no value, or fewer prints than a bucket needs).

Mean reaction vs the market of the same industry's prints that reacted in the prior 35 days (the name excluded), and how many there were (at least 3 for a value): how the market is paying this industry's prints this season. Measured as a pointer like the others.

A $5,000 starter (recipe starter_usd) times the set-up cell's 10th / 90th percentile reaction vs the market (setup_rx_q10 / q90): the overnight bad and good case in dollars of buying before the print; the same for every name in one set-up cell. own_move_starter_usd = the starter times the name's own mean absolute past reaction (react_abs_mean): its typical move either way. Size reads, not stops.

What the alpha model's decile the name sits in today returned out of sample (mean excess, share positive) at that horizon (alpha_model deciles.csv). Read with state_<h>: a FAILING or WEAK horizon's decile is context, not a lean.
The alpha model horizon's health from its out-of-sample record (OK, WEAK, DEGRADED, FAILING, NO_TRACK).

True when the name is in the US panel store today, so its pointer values come from the same store features the past prints were measured on; false = values from the earnings-week calendar where a field exists (Europe and names off the store floor).
TradingView market of the listing (america, germany, uk, ...).

One line per reporter built from the pack: the set-up into the print, forward P/E against the industry and its own median, the 28-day / 7-day pointer counts, its average print move (after the print: the mix, the surprises, the reaction).

Going into the print: run-up, month, quarter, distance to the 50-day, RSI, place in the 52-week range; the previous print and how many past prints rose; the set-up cell's measured hold and overnight tail; the deterioration cell and letters beyond price.

Forward P/E against the industry median and its own median, EV/EBITDA against the industry, FCF and operating margins, net debt / EBITDA, the street target (range, one-month drift), margin of safety to its own P/E median and to peers.

What the quarter has to show: consensus EPS and revenue against last quarter's reported numbers, next-FY EPS revisions and the quintile of past prints they sit in (with that cell's measured 28-day hold lift), last quarter's surprise and mix, growth.

The industry's US $2B+ peers (outlook names): median forward P/E, month and quarter, the name's month rank, the largest peers; the industry's prints in the prior 35 days (count, mean reaction vs the market, how many rose, the latest); peers printing the same session.

The print-night pointer counts and lists per horizon (28-day, 7-day hold, reaction), the alpha model's 7d / 28d deciles with the decile's measured return and state, the model's 28-day drivers, the industry's season reaction.
The buy-in-red band and its kill, the 50-day band and its kill, the first target, the starter's overnight bad case and own typical move in dollars, and the Book position.
The name's past prints from the day files, newest first: date, slot, reaction, EPS surprise.

After the print: the surprises, the mix (and whether revenue is posted), the after-hours or session move, the mix cell's measured reaction and drift lift, the print pointers, the set-up x reaction cell.

What to read on the print: the quarter's bar, the measured mix and after-hours cells, the slot and set-up notes (recipe text from the earnings playbook), the starter's overnight size, the down pointers.
The industry's US $2B+ peers in the outlook (the name excluded): how many, their median forward P/E (positive only), month and quarter, percent.
The name's trailing-month rank among its industry peers (1 = the best month).
How many of the session's reporters are in the industry, and which.
The industry's lab prints that reacted in the prior 35 days: how many, their mean reaction vs the market (pp), the share that rose, the latest four (id, MM-DD, reaction).
True when the Book line sits in the recipe cluster (theme industries + ids: AI build-out industries, hyperscalers, NASDAQ:GOOG).
Slope of the line's store steps (close to close between day files) on the cap-weighted US floor's step: how many % the line moved per 1% of the market, measured in the store (since 29 Mar 2026).
beta_store measured only on steps where the cap-weighted market fell: the line's sensitivity in down sessions.
TradingView 1-year beta (for a non-US line: against its home market; XETR:VUAA set to 1, it tracks the S&P 500).
The beta the scenarios use: beta_store, else beta_tv, else 1 (beta_src says which).
Where beta_used came from: store (measured), tv (TradingView, line not in the US store), one (no beta).
Correlation of the line's store steps with the cap-weighted market step (1 = moves with the market every session).
Store steps (day-file pairs) the line has; the betas need at least the recipe's beta_min_steps.
One-month volatility: standard deviation of the line's store steps x sqrt(21), %. One sigma, so about 1 month in 6 moves more than this down.
The line's own 5th-percentile 28-day return in the store (1 window in 20 was at or under it), %.
The line's worst 28-day return in the store, %.
The line's deepest peak-to-trough drawdown inside the store (since 29 Mar 2026), %.
The line now against its store high, %.
The level against the close, % (negative = the level is under the close: the fall to it; positive = already under the level).
mkt<k>_usd: the line's dollars if the cap-weighted US market falls k% (value x beta_used x -k%). Linear: a cluster shock runs past it.
Scenario: the cap-weighted US floor's move (an S&P 500-like index), %.
The Book's dollars in the scenario at store beta (_store), down-session beta (_down) or TradingView beta (_tv).
That loss as % of NAV (equity + cash).
The cluster lines' share of the scenario loss, $.
Window length in calendar days (start file to the first file at least that far).
cap = cap-weighted US floor ($2B+, an S&P 500-like index); med = the median name; cluster = cap-weighted cluster names; book = today's Book with today's dollars held through the window.
Windows (overlapping, one per start file) behind the row.
qNN_pct: NN-th percentile of the window returns, % (q05 = 1 window in 20 was at or under it; q50 the median).
The Book's qNN window in dollars (today's values).
The worst window return, %; worst_start = the file it started on.
Start file of the worst window.
The Book's worst window in dollars (today's values).
p_le_k: share of windows that fell k% or more (0.10 = 1 window in 10).
Mean window return, %.
Drawdown id: series_rank (cap_1 = the cap-weighted market's deepest store drawdown).
Store file of the high before the drawdown.
Store file of the low.
Peak-to-trough fall of the episode's series, %.
First file back at the old high; empty = still under it.
Today's Book over that window, % of equity.
Today's Book over that window, % of NAV.
The cap-weighted market, the median name and the cluster over the same window, %.
The line's dollars over the window (today's value x ret_pct).
Steps in the window where the line had no store close and took beta x the market step.
Series under its running store high, % (book: today's Book held at today's weights).
Book dollars in lines without a store step at that step (beta x market used).
Names on the floor (cluster) in the step.
Window start and end files.
Store step end file (the step runs from as_of to nxt).
to_<level>_usd: the line's dollars if it moves from the close to that level (value x to_<level>_pct).
Odds of a further -10% (raw) within 56 days in the line's drawdown x letters x market-regime cell (deterioration).
The capital plan a row belongs to: capital_plan (today), capital_plan_queue (later, in band), capital_plan_derisk (triggered), capital_plan_pathway.
Dollars the plan row moves on the line (value after - value now; negative = sold).
delta_usd x beta_used: the market exposure the row adds (+) or removes (-), in beta dollars.
The entry book's target split by source: exit_target_street = the street price target, exit_target_pack = the pack's own target; exit_target is whichever the band used (target_source).

Fair value today under the bear / base / bull path (financial_projection value run): dividends and the year-5 price (EPS x exit P/E, or EV/Sales for loss makers) discounted at hurdle_pct. Year 1 is the street's revenue and EPS forecast.
Scenario-weighted fair value today (bear 25% / base 50% / bull 25%, recipe weights): one measure under three paths, not a score.
fv_exp_px against the close, %. The model level is conservative (median about -11%): compare names, not to zero.
Annual return the path pays from today's price (dividends + year-5 price), %; _exp on the scenario-weighted cash flows.
Cost of equity used to discount: risk-free 4.75% + beta (clipped 0.6-2.0) x 5% equity premium, %.
irr_exp_pct minus hurdle_pct, points: the mispricing read (positive = the price buys more than the name's required return).
Reverse solve: the constant 5-year revenue CAGR at which the base path's fair value equals today's price, %.
Base-path revenue CAGR minus priced_in_cagr_pct, points: growth the path expects beyond what the price needs.
Value lens: earnings (exit P/E on year-5 EPS) or sales (exit EV/Sales on year-5 revenue less net debt, loss makers).
Value-run flags: currency_mismatch, implausible_pe, <scenario>_multiple_capped, y1_growth_above_cap, pe_under_half_industry (often cyclical peak earnings), net_debt_over_mcap, <scenario>_set_to_base.
EPS on the value run's base path: year 1 = the street's next-FY EPS; year 5 after decaying growth and margin convergence.
FCF-to-equity DCF cross-check on the base path (5 years + a 3% terminal growth), per share and % vs the close; none for Finance.
Earnings week from the scan day: W0 this week, W1 next week.

The name's positioning today on the beat-bar grid axes: run-up into the print (%, 14 days), the trailing three months (%), the next-FY EPS estimate change over three months (%). Same definitions the past prints were cut on.

Positioning cell: the tercile (T1 low, T2 middle, T3 high) of each axis on the lab's past prints, e.g. runup:T1 & r_3m:T1 & eps_rev_3m:T1 = sold into the print, down over three months, estimates cut (a low bar). Edges in PACK/beat_bar/overview.log.
0 = the full three-axis cell; 1-3 = a fallback axis set (recipe grid.fallbacks) because the full cell had too few beats or misses or the name lacks an axis value.
Past prints in the cell that beat (EPS surprise > 0) / missed. The reads below rest on these counts.
Mean reaction-session move vs the market (pp) of the cell's beats / misses. What a beat paid and a miss cost in this set-up.
Share of the cell's beats / misses whose reaction beat the market (0-1).
Share of the cell's beats that fell vs the market on the reaction session: how often a beat was not what the market wanted (base 0.45).
c_rx_beat minus c_rx_miss (pp): how much the outcome of the print mattered in this set-up.
Mean reaction vs the market (pp) of the cell's EPS beats that also beat revenue (B/B) / missed revenue (B/M): whether revenue had to beat too.
A beat in this cell minus a beat in every other cell (pp) and its Welch t. Positive = beats paid more here than elsewhere. Prints cluster by date: the t is optimistic.
The beat lift in each half of the sample (split at the median print date). A lift that holds in both halves is sturdier; few early prints carry a three-month axis.

The bar: the lowest EPS-surprise quintile (edges on every lab print: -3.7, +3.3, +9.7, +24.0%) whose mean reaction in the cell was positive. 'EPS surprise >= -3.7%' = anything but a deep miss was paid; '>= +24.0%' = only a very large beat was paid.
Hold-through excess (pp) from the pre-print close, 7 / 28 days, of the cell's beats / misses: what owning into the print and holding returned.
Beat odds used for the mix: (own beats in the store + 4 x the cell's beat rate) / (own prints + 4). Thin own history leans on the cell. A measured frequency, not a forecast of this quarter.

p_beat x the cell's beat hit rate + (1 - p_beat) x its miss hit rate: the measured odds of beating the market on the reaction (or the 7 / 28-day hold). A mix of frequencies, never a gate, size or sort key.
p_beat x the cell's beat mean + (1 - p_beat) x its miss mean (pp vs the market): the reaction / 7-day / 28-day hold read mixed by the beat odds. Not a score.
A $5,000 starter times the cell's 90th-percentile beat reaction / 10th-percentile miss reaction: the good and bad overnight case in dollars. Size reads, not stops.

Pre-print pointers whose quintile (the one the name sits in) made beats pay more / less than other beats on the reaction, with the print-night rule (|t| >= 2, n >= 40, both halves, hit rate the same way). Counts are cells, not a score.
The name's own EPS surprises (%) on its prints in the panel store, oldest first.
12-month return bucket at the start: 12M down, 12M 0-50, 12M 50-100, 12M 100+ (%). 12M 100+ in a drawdown is the crowded-winner unwind state.
Which of the line's cells fills the p_<need>_<d> / days_<need> / floor columns: cnt (drawdown x letter count) when the line has a count cell, else dd (drawdown only).

Which recovery-clock study the row reads: dd = drawdown bucket only; cnt = drawdown x letter count (starts from July, when 3-month revisions exist, so its long checkpoints stay empty); run = drawdown x 12-month run; mkt = drawdown x the median name's trailing month.
The cell label: the state keys joined by ' | ' in study order (for example 'dd 20-35 | 12M 100+').

The rise from today's close to the level, %: cost = the line's average price, gain10 = cost +10%, sma50 = the 50-day average, half = half-way back to the 52-week high, street = the street target, high = the 52-week high. 0 or less = already there.
The level a reach row asks about: cost, gain10, sma50, half, street, high (see need_<level>_pct).

Kaplan-Meier odds (0-1) that a start in the same cell closed at or above that rise at least once by day d (calendar days), on the panel store. Starts the store stopped seeing count while seen. Empty when fewer than 40 starts (10 names) were observed through day d. A touch, not a hold: the close can fall back after.
Median calendar days for a start in the cell to first close at or above that rise (the day the Kaplan-Meier odds pass one half). Empty when fewer than half got there inside the store.

The lowest close inside the next W days against the start close, %, over complete windows: med = the typical path low, q25 / q10 = the bad quarter / bad tenth. The dip you sit through, not where it ends.
That path low applied to the line: the price (quote currency) and the USD change on the line's value.
Share of complete windows whose path low fell k% or more under the start inside W days (0-1).
Median calendar days from the start to the lowest close inside W days.
The close W calendar days after the start against the start close, % (raw, winsorized 1%): median, mean, bad tenth, good tenth. Where the cell ended, not its path.
fwd_W minus the median start of that same day, pp: what staying in this cell earned over the median name (mean), and the share of starts that beat it (hit).
Complete W-day windows behind the window reads, and the distinct names among them. Starts are weekly, so one name appears many times: names is the honest count.
Distinct names and start days behind a cell.

The line's value x the cell's fx_91_mean: what the cell's average excess over the median name was worth on this line over 91 days. Negative = staying cost money against the median name. A frequency, not a forecast.
Recovery ladder scenario: the level the add is bought at (close, bounce_high, bounce_low), its price (quote currency) and the USD added.
The bounce kill (bounce_kill) the ladder measures the add's loss to.
EPS over the last twelve months and the street's next-fiscal-year EPS (year 1 of the path; TTM x revenue growth when the street EPS is missing), quote currency.
The boom pace: the larger of the street's year-1 EPS growth and revenue growth (%). Each extra boom year grows at this pace halved per year, between the recipe floor (0%) and cap (30%).
Close / street year-1 EPS: the forward P/E the cycle path starts from.
Close / the peak EPS if the boom lasts k more years after year 1 (k2 = peak in year 3). Low = the price is a small multiple of boom earnings. pe_on_peak (grid) = the same for the row's k.
Year-1 net margin implied by the street EPS (%), the industry median net margin (%), and their ratio. A ratio far above 1 in a cyclical industry = peak-cycle margins.

The peak-to-trough EPS drop (% of the peak) that today's close already pays for after k boom years, at the 15x through-cycle exit. 100 = EPS to zero for a year, then back to half the peak. Empty = needs_more (even no bust is not enough) or covers_max (survives a 150% drop).

The exit P/E on normalized EPS at year 5 that today's close requires after k boom years and an EPS drop of d% (normalized = peak x (1 - d/2)). Compare with a through-cycle multiple (memory has been paid about 10-15x, the market about 15-20x): far above = the price needs the boom to keep going.
The fewest extra boom years (0-3) whose value at a 15x exit covers today's close if a d% bust follows. Empty = more than 3 years.
Scenario value at the 15x exit against today's close (%), after k boom years and a d% EPS drop. A value gap, not a price forecast.
Grid row: extra boom years after year 1, and the EPS drop from the peak (%).
Through-cycle exit P/E on the normalized EPS: 10, 15, or ind = the industry median forward P/E (clipped 6-35).
The path: the year EPS peaks (1 + k), the peak, the trough (peak x (1 - d)) and the normalized level it recovers to (peak x (1 - d/2)).
Five years of path EPS added up, as % of today's close: 100 = the business earns its price back in five years even through the bust.
Close / normalized EPS: today's price on through-cycle earnings.
Scenario value today (owner cash at 0.8 x EPS a year plus the exit, discounted at the hurdle) and the annual return the path pays from today's close (%).
EPS year 1 to year 5 on the scenario path, slash-separated.
Beta-based cost of equity from the forward value run (risk-free + beta x 5% premium), the discount rate of the path (%).

Stress: the scenario's price move on the line (%; a judgment input, OUTSIDE analogs), the line's role in the AI chain, and the dollars as % of NAV. BOOK total row (empty symbol): shock_pct = the dollar-weighted move of the whole Book.
Forward value run: close / street next-FY EPS, and the industry median forward P/E.
Peer-value lens the row's primary read uses: pe = forward P/E (100 / next-FY EPS yield), evebitda = EV / EBITDA, evs = EV / sales (the first present in that order).
The name's multiple on the lens and its peer group's median multiple (the industry, the sector when the industry is thin). peer_mult in the peers table = that peer's multiple on the same lens.
Premium of the multiple to the peer median, %. Negative = a plain discount to peers.

The premium (or discount) the name's growth and quality earn inside its group: the group's ridge fit of the log multiple on z-scored drivers (revenue / EPS growth next FY, margins, ROE, revisions), as % vs the median.

Fitted vs actual multiple, %: positive = cheaper than peers with the same growth / quality get; negative = paying more than the profile earns. Not a target: cyclicals at peak margins and names classified into the wrong industry fit badly.
The price at the peer-fitted multiple (close x fitted / actual multiple). A peer-relative level, kept apart from street, pack and model prices.

Percentile inside the peer group, 0-100: value on the forward EPS yield (high = cheap), growth = next-FY revenue growth, eps_growth = next-FY EPS growth, quality = operating margin, roe, fcf = FCF margin, revision = 3-month EPS estimate change.
The name minus its peer group's median, in the field's own unit (percentage points for growth, margins, ROE, revisions).
Forward P/E / next-FY EPS growth (%), and its % vs the group median PEG. Empty when EPS growth is not positive.

The forward value run's priced-in revenue CAGR / expected IRR / fair-value upside / growth gap minus the peer group's median, pp: a priced-in growth above peers' is a premium the price already asks for.
The peer group: 'ind: <TradingView industry>' or 'sector: <sector>' when the industry has too few names; group_kind says which.
Nearest peers: the peer's market cap / the name's, and its rank by distance in log market cap.
The same read for the peer in the nearest-peers table.
Group fit: % change in the multiple per one standard deviation of the driver (what the group pays for), R2 of the fit, and whether the group had enough names to fit.

Peer-value evidence: daily Spearman IC of a signal (gap_pct, disc_pct = -prem_pct, pe_gap_pct) with the forward return minus that day's median name, its t on independent periods (span / horizon), the share of days it was positive, and quantile means (5 = highest signal).
The row is a Book line / an id named on the command line.
Next-FY revenue growth vs TTM (%) and return on equity (%), the name's own value beside its peer's.

Where the close sits against the bounce band: below_kill (under bounce_kill), under_band (between the kill and bounce_low), in_band, over_band (above bounce_high). A position label, not a signal; the band is priced under the close, so over_band is the usual state.
Bounce band top vs the close, %: the fall needed for a resting order at the band top to fill (negative = the close is above the band).
Bounce kill vs the close, %: the distance to the price where the entry thesis fails.

The beat-bar positioning cell of a W0 / W1 reporter: terciles (T1 low, T3 high) of the run-up into the print, the 3-month tape and the 3-month EPS estimate change on the lab's past prints; fewer axes when the cell fell back (config/generic_utils/beat_bar.json).

bb_cell split per axis: bar_runup = run-up into the print, bar_tape = 3-month return, bar_rev = 3-month next-FY EPS estimate change, each as its tercile T1 / T2 / T3 on the lab's past prints. Low bar = bar_rev T1 with bar_tape T1; high bar = both T3. Empty when the cell did not use the axis.
Tercile of a beat-bar axis on the lab's past prints: T1 = lowest third (estimates cut, weakest tape, sold into the print), T2 = middle, T3 = highest third.
Share of the cell's past prints that beat the EPS estimate.
The name's own last prints read by the beat bar (own_n) and how many of them beat (own_beats).

Winners-anatomy pattern letters the name carries today: pat_up from OBIDHVCL (up patterns), pat_dn from XYZ (down patterns); rules in config/generic_utils/anatomy.json. Read the anatomy month table before using one.
How many of the name's up letters are in the anatomy's durable set (OBIDH: patterns that held across months).
Percentile of the 3-month EPS estimate change inside the peer group (100 = rising fastest), peer value.
EPS growth on the last reported year vs the year before, %.
Day move of the US $2B+ floor, market-cap weighted, % at the file's scan time.
Day move of the median name on the floor, %.
Cap-weighted index return over the last 5 / 21 store files (sessions), %.
ret_cap minus ret_med, pp: positive = megacaps carry the day (narrow), negative = the median name leads.
The deepest cap-index drawdown from its store high over the previous 10 files, %.
Share of floor names up on the day, %.
10-file mean of adv_pct / upvol_pct, %.
Share of floor names closing over their 50-day / 200-day average, %.
Share of floor names within 2% of their 52-week high / low, %.
nh_pct minus nl_pct, pp.
Share of the floor's traded volume in names up on the day, % (a ratio: holds on an intraday scan).
Floor volume so far over its 30-day average volume (not scaled for the time of day).
vol_ratio divided by scan_frac: the day's volume pace against the 30-day average (rough on intraday files).
1 = vol_pace above the file before, 0 = below.
1 = a distribution day (cap index down 0.2%+ with vol_up) / an accumulation day (up 0.2%+ with vol_up).
Distribution / accumulation days over the last 25 files.
Median RSI(14) across the floor.
Share of floor names with RSI(14) at 70+ / at 30 or under, %.
Cross-sectional standard deviation of the day's moves, pp.
Median opening gap across the floor, %.
Median TradingView relative volume across the floor.
Mean day move of the highest-beta third minus the lowest-beta third (and its 10-file mean), pp: risk appetite.
Mean day move of the prior file's top 1-month third minus its bottom third (and its 10-file mean), pp: momentum working or unwinding.
Mean day move of the defensive sectors (utilities, consumer non-durables, health services) minus all names (and its 10-file mean), pp.
AI cluster (ai_buildout + hyperscalers industries, GOOG) cap-weighted day move minus the floor's (and its 5-file sum), pp.
Prints (US $2B+) whose reaction landed in the last 10 files / how many of them beat on EPS.
Mean reaction-session move of those beats / misses, %.
Share of those beats that fell on the reaction session, %.
Share of floor names with next-FY EPS estimates / price targets raised over a month minus the share cut, pp.
Share of floor names with a positive TradingView technical rating, %.
Median move-prediction exhaustion / fragility / breakout score across the floor (store pred).
Market timing policy run of that day: ENTER_SMALL + ENTER_PROBE as a share of its book, %. Climate, never a buy list.
Names in that day's market timing policy book.
UTC time of the day file's scan.
Share of the US cash session seen at scan_at (1 = after the close; floor 0.15).
Daily series: the cap index's return over the next h files (sessions), %. Patterns: the mean of that return after a match.
A market sentiment reading (a column of the daily series).
What the reading measures and how it is read.
The reading now minus five files ago.
Today's value as a percentile of the reading's store history (0 = lowest, 100 = highest).
Today's quintile of the reading's store history (1 = lowest fifth, 5 = highest).
Rank correlation (Spearman) of the reading with the cap index's next-h-file return over the store's days.
The same IC in the first / second half of the store's days: both must agree before an arrow.
t of ic_<h> with n_indep = days / h (overlapping windows counted once).
Independent windows behind ic_<h>: days / h.
Days in today's quintile with a known forward return / their mean next-h-file cap return, %.
Mean next-h-file cap return over all days, %.
Readings: today's quintile mean minus all days (cell_fwd minus base_fwd), pp. Patterns: the mean after a match minus all days, pp.
up / down when the reading cleared the arrow rule at that horizon; empty otherwise.

▲ / ▼ with lift_<h> when the measured relation cleared its rule (|t| >= 2, n_indep >= 5, both halves agree, today's percentile leans, the quintile's lift agrees); a bare number = the quintile's lift without a clear direction.
Readings in the family.
Readings in the family with a measured up / down arrow at that horizon. Counted, never summed into a score.
The readings behind up_<h> / dn_<h>.
A named technical pattern: a condition on the daily series (recipe market_sentiment.json patterns).
true = today's file matches the pattern.
Files that matched / separate runs of consecutive matches (episodes are the real sample size).
Patterns: matched days with a known next-h-file return / the share of them positive, %.
The pattern's condition on the daily series columns.
OUTSIDE: readings of that kind so far / today's percentile in its own recorded history (10+ readings) / the change from the previous reading.
OUTSIDE: the value's unit, the source link, and the OUTSIDE tag (timing and Grade only).

Event-risk level of the line (tv_scan_cli.py event-risk, recipe config/generic_utils/event_risk.json): the first of WARN_STRONG, WARN, WATCH whose rule letters are all on (warn_rule); empty = none. A review trigger for the judgment, not a course, not a size and not a score.

Event-risk level: a mapped event ahead with big dollars at stress (E$), an event that already repriced the crowd with big dollars (R$), a market-wide binary event ahead on a high-beta, gap-prone line with big dollars (PBT$), or an industry shock on a high-beta line with big dollars (SB$). The Reason must say what the line does about it (hold through, trim, hedge, exit) and why.

Event-risk level: a mapped event ahead (E), an event that already repriced the crowd (R), a binary event on a high-beta line with big dollars (PB$), an industry shock on a high-beta line (SB) or with a gap-prone line and big dollars (ST$). Review the line; no forced action.
The rule alternative (letter string) that set warn_level, e.g. R$ = an event repriced the crowd and the stress costs at least 1% of NAV.

Event-risk letters, recipe order E P R U S B T V D $, only the ones on; - = none. E = a calendar event in the next 10 days names the line (symbols) or maps its theme / 40%+ of its crowd's cap to the down or either side. P = a market-wide binary event (kind policy or binary: true, no symbols) in the next 10 days that does not map the line: direction unknown, the size is the risk. R / U = a policy, binary or mapped event in the last 5 days moved the line's crowd with z <= -2 (R) / >= +2 (U) on its step. S = the line's industry (cap-weighted, without the line) 5-step z <= -2. B = beta to that industry over 40 steps >= 1.2. T = own worst step in the last 60 <= -8%. V = forward-value fv_upside_pct < 0 and irr_exp_pct < hurdle_pct (price set for the boom). D = deterioration letters beyond price. $ = stress_5s_usd costs at least 1% of NAV (held lines only).

Event-risk stress on the line: the worse of (its crowd's worst 5-step move in the store x its down-beta to the crowd) and (its own worst 5-step move), %; _usd = held value x that / 100, _nav = % of NAV. A measured bad week, not a forecast; stress_src says which side set it.

Which series set the stress: crowd (the correlated crowd), industry (no crowd cleared the correlation floor, so the industry without the line stood in), own (the line's own worst 5-step move was worse).
Parts of the stress: crowd's worst 5-step (1-step) move x down-beta, and the line's own worst 5-step move, %.

The line's crowd: the up to 15 US $2B+ names whose store steps correlated most with its own over the last 90 steps (each at corr >= 0.35; share classes and ADR twins skipped), the largest six shown; crowd_n = members, crowd_corr = their mean correlation.
The crowd's cap-weighted move on the last store step, the last 5 and 21 steps, and its drawdown from its store high, %.
The crowd's last step over the sd of its prior 60 steps (crowd_z); the last 5 steps over that sd x sqrt(5) (crowd_z5); the same for the line's industry without it (ind_z5, the S letter at <= -2).
OLS beta of the line's store steps on its crowd's (all steps / crowd-down steps), and on its industry without it over the last 40 steps (the B letter at >= 1.2).

The crowd's worst 1-step and 5-step move in the store; capture_pct = the line's mean step on the crowd's worst 5% steps (n = capture_n); own_worst_pct = the line's worst step in the last 60 (the T letter at <= -8%); own_day_pct = its last step.

Calendar (OUTSIDE, config/generic_utils/catalyst_calendar.json): the nearest event in the next 10 days that maps the line (side down / up / either, how: symbol, theme, crowd share), the nearest market-wide binary event that does not map it, and the latest OUTSIDE odds linked to the event (odds_kind). Timing and Grade only.
The policy / binary / mapped event in the last 5 days whose step moved the crowd most (|z| >= 2): the event, the crowd's z and move on that step, and the line's own move.
The line's measured S / B / T combination (none = no letter), the key of its evidence row.

Point-in-time evidence of the S / B / T state on the store: mean (median) raw forward return less the file's median over 7 / 28 calendar days, t on the per-file means, p_dn = share with a raw 28-day return <= -15%, q10 = the 10th percentile, n_files / n_indep = files / 20. Months of store, not cycles: read n_indep first.
After an industry crash step (1-step z <= -2.5): the industry's next 1 / 5 / 20 steps less the median industry's, %; n_crashes on n_dates distinct steps.

Event reactions / events: the store file a step ends on, the calendar events landing on it (none is credited alone), each industry's move and z on it, the Book lines in that industry; events: window (ahead / recent), binary (policy or binary: true), market_wide (binary with no symbols), credited (counts for R / U), exposure map and odds.
The price a focus-book ticket is judged from: the lower of the close and the top of the bounce band (bounce_high). A close above the band means waiting for the band, not buying the close.

Month upside from entry_px, %: the lower of the alpha model's 28-day q80 band (b28d_q80) and the street target (street_px), over entry_px, minus 1. The model's good case capped by the street, not a forecast.
Distance from entry_px down to the kill on a close, %: the bounce kill (bounce_kill), else the entry book's kill_px. What the ticket loses if the kill prints, before slippage.

Up / risk: month_up_pct divided by risk_pct (2.0 = two points of month upside per point of risk to the kill). A ratio of two separate reads for ordering one lane; not a score, never summed with rr, bo or the model.
1 when the name's industry is in the ai_buildout theme's industries (config/generic_utils/themes.json), else 0. In late 2026 those names trade as one contagion crowd and are kept in their own lane.

How drop_in_k<k> was found: solved (a drop between 0 and 150% matches the close), needs_more (even no bust is not enough: the price needs the boom to keep going), covers_max (the close survives a 150% drop).
The street's year-1 EPS growth used to start the cycle path, % (next fiscal year EPS over trailing EPS).
